commit.message:
Stop label line merging from taking quadratic time (#8436)

* perf: merge line labels by linking the lines instead of copying them

mergeLines concatenated the whole accumulated line on every merge, so a tile
whose `symbol-placement: line` features chain end to end paid a copy of
everything merged so far for each new line. The cost grew with the square of
the chain length, which is the common shape for trail, river and street data
where one named way arrives as many short features.

A merged line is now a linked list of the input lines, so a merge is a pointer
update, and the points are copied into one right-sized array at the end. The
joint point that `pop`/`shift` used to drop is skipped while joining instead.

Median of 40 runs, lines of 24 points each, label text supplied as `Formatted`
so `toString` allocates per call as it does in a real bucket. The two
implementations alternate within a run so drift cannot favour either:

  one label, 250 features     0.89ms -> 0.19ms    (4.6x)
  one label, 1000 features   18.6ms  -> 0.90ms     (21x)
  one label, 4000 features  325ms    -> 3.76ms     (86x)

The ratio grows with the chain because the chain is what the removed term was
squared over. Where nothing merges the two are level, 3.95ms against 3.87ms at
4000 features: this commit only removes copying that merging caused.

The output was compared against the previous implementation over 15000
randomly generated inputs.

* docs: add the changelog entry

* refactor: hoist the merge helpers and use Record for the endpoint indexes

Address review: the merge helpers no longer close over the loop state,
and the chain tests use literal point lists instead of generated ones.
